title: Discrete mathematics
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the mathematics of computer science: propositional and predicate logic, proof techniques, induction, sets, functions and relations, counting, discrete probability, number theory and modular arithmetic, graphs and trees, and recurrences.
primary_reading: MIT OpenCourseWare 6.042J: Mathematics for Computer Science (free textbook and lectures)

weeks.3: Proof techniques: direct, contrapositive and contradiction
weeks.7: Counting: sum and product rules, permutations and combinations
weeks.10: Number theory: divisibility, gcd and modular arithmetic
weeks.11: Graphs: paths, connectivity and Euler tours

blocks.deliverable: Translate statements into logic and prove equivalences with truth tables.
Write five proofs, two of them by induction.
Classify functions as injective, surjective or bijective.
Week 7 midterm; solve ten counting problems.
Compute modular inverses and apply them.
Prove a property of trees and solve a recurrence.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Proof portfolio and application: write up ten carefully proved results from the course, then use modular arithmetic to explain RSA encryption and carry it out on small numbers by hand and in code.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
